CellEdgeR

Differential analysis of cell-type interaction motifs from spatial coordinates.

Overview

CellEdgeR builds per-sample Delaunay graphs, counts label-based motifs, and fits edgeR models with Chung-Lu-style volume offsets. Volume normalization is the main statistical model.

The tested result sets are:

  • top_edges(): edge motifs, keyed as E_<label1>_<label2>.
  • top_motifs2(): wedge and triangle motifs, keyed as W_<center>_<leaf1>_<leaf2> and T_<label1>_<label2>_<label3>.

Node counts are still computed internally to build exposures and normalized submotif values, but nodes are not tested as differential motifs. Wedges and triangles are not merged into TP_* triplets.

Installation 

install.packages(c("geometry", "Matrix"))
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
if (!requireNamespace("edgeR", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("edgeR")

devtools::install_github("GeNeHetX/CellEdgeR")
library(CellEdgeR)

Typical Workflow

  1. Prepare a named list of samples. Each element is a data frame with numeric x, y coordinates and a cell label column.
samples_list <- make_demo_samples(n_cells = 10000, seed = 42)

metadata_df <- data.frame(
  condition = rep(c("ctrl", "treated"), each = length(samples_list) / 2),
  batch = sample(c("batch1", "batch2"), length(samples_list), replace = TRUE),
  row.names = names(samples_list)
)
  1. Build graphs and count motifs.
cellgraph <- build_cell_graphs(samples_list, n_cores = 4, verbose = TRUE)
cellgraph <- count_motifs_graphs(
  cellgraph,
  max_edge_len = 50,
  include_wedge = TRUE,
  n_cores = 4
)

count_motifs_graphs() stores raw counts, volume exposures, volume offsets, normalized counts, and relative counts. The stored offset mode is volume.

  1. Fit the differential model and extract the two result tables.
cellgraph <- motif_edger(
  cellgraph = cellgraph,
  sample_df = metadata_df,
  design_formula = "~ condition + batch"
)

results <- motif_results(cellgraph, coef = "conditiontreated")
edges_tbl <- results$edges
motifs2_tbl <- results$motifs2

head(edges_tbl)
head(motifs2_tbl)

motifs2_tbl includes the wedge/triangle result plus edge-submotif columns: edge12, edge13, edge23, their logFC/PValue/FDR, and summary columns submotif_min_FDR and submotif_max_abs_logFC.

Before fitting, motif_edger() applies edgeR::filterByExpr() to the stacked edge/wedge/triangle count matrix. One-off motifs or motifs with too little support are not tested and therefore do not receive p-values or FDR values. Filter details are stored in cellgraph$edger$filter.

  1. Inspect normalized counts or spatial motif plots.
norm_df <- get_motif_values(cellgraph, value = "norm")
head(norm_df)

plot_sample_graph(
  cellgraph,
  sample_name = "s1",
  max_edge_len = 50,
  motif_key = "T_a_b_c",
  motif_node_size = 0.8,
  dim_node_nonmotif = 0.1,
  alpha_node_nonmotif = 0.2,
  alpha_edge_nonmotif = 0.2
)

Choosing A Pruning Threshold

The max_edge_len threshold controls which Delaunay edges are retained before motif counting. Inspect the edge-length distribution and drop the sparse tail while preserving biologically relevant local neighbors.

edge_lengths <- unlist(lapply(cellgraph$per_sample_graph, function(ps) ps$edge_len))
summary(edge_lengths)

ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(edge_len = edge_lengths), ggplot2::aes(edge_len)) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(fill = "#4477aa", alpha = 0.3, color = "#223355") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10("Edge length (log scale)") +
  ggplot2::ylab("Density") +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Edge length distribution (density, log-x)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

Statistical Model

CellEdgeR uses volume offsets as a Chung-Lu-style exposure correction:

  • Edges use label degree volumes and the sample total edge volume.
  • Triangles use the three label volumes and unordered-label multiplicity.
  • Wedges use center-label degree-pair exposure plus leaf-label volumes, with an equal-leaf correction.

The edgeR QL model tests differential motif rates after this exposure correction. This is not a simple test of raw or normalized boxplot medians.

Tips

  • Use include_wedge = TRUE when you want both wedges and triangles in top_motifs2().
  • Provide boundary/is_boundary columns or erosion_cells if boundary motifs should be excluded.
  • Record max_edge_len and offset_version from cellgraph$parameters for reproducibility.
  • Use get_motif_values(cellgraph, value = "norm", include_submotifs = TRUE) to plot a motif with its edge submotifs.
  • Use motif_space_size() to summarize the possible tested edge/wedge/triangle label space.

Main Functions

  • build_cell_graphs(): Build per-sample Delaunay graphs from coordinates and labels.
  • count_motifs_graphs(): Count node, edge, triangle, and optional wedge motifs and compute volume offsets.
  • merge_motif_objs(): Merge motif objects and recompute volume offsets.
  • motif_edger(): Fit the volume-offset edgeR model.
  • top_edges(): Return ranked edge motifs.
  • top_motifs2(): Return ranked wedge and triangle motifs with edge-submotif statistics.
  • motif_results(): Return edges and motifs2 in one named list.
  • get_motif_values(): Return raw or volume-normalized motif values.
  • plot_sample_graph(): Plot one sample graph and highlight a motif.
